name: ontology_tutorial
description: Reproduce the Microsoft Fabric ontology (preview) tutorial end-to-end with fabio: build the Lakeshore Retail lakehouse + eventhouse, generate an ontology from a semantic model (or import one), enrich it with time-series data, and consume it with a data agent and natural-language queries. Mirrors https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/ontology/tutorial-0-introduction.

steps.step: Create the lakehouse and load the static tables
commands: fabio lakehouse load-table --workspace <WS> --id <LH> --table dimproducts --path Files/DimProducts.csv --format Csv
# repeat upload+load-table for DimStore, FactSales, Freezer (table names lowercased)
steps.notes: Do NOT load FreezerTelemetry.csv here — it goes to the eventhouse (streaming/time-series).

steps.step: Create the eventhouse + KQL table and ingest the telemetry
steps.notes: The eventhouse auto-creates a KQL database of the same name. The FreezerTelemetry table has a timestamp column used for time-series binding.

steps.step: Build the ontology — Option A: generate from a semantic model (portal-parity, client-side)
commands: # create a Direct Lake semantic model over the lakehouse tables first (semantic-model create --file <model> --connection <sql-endpoint-id>), then:
steps.notes: generate reads the model's tables/columns/relationships via INFO.VIEW, synthesizes entity types + typed properties + relationship types + keys, and (with --lakehouse) binds each entity to its same-named lakehouse table. This reproduces the portal's 'Generate Ontology' (which has no REST API). Inspect first with --output-owl <file>.

steps.step: Build the ontology — Option B: build directly from OneLake (no semantic model)
steps.notes: Author an OWL/TTL schema (entity types + properties + relationships) and a bindings map (entity->table), or bootstrap OWL from a tenant scan: fabio context tenant --format owl.

steps.step: Enrich the ontology with time-series (eventhouse) data
steps.notes: Bind the Freezer entity's time-series properties (temperatureC, humidityPct, doorOpen) from the FreezerTelemetry eventhouse table. An entity can carry BOTH a static lakehouse binding and a time-series eventhouse binding.
list-entity-types reproduces the ontology MCP server's list_ontology_entity_types tool offline (schema exploration).

steps.step: Consume the ontology with a data agent + natural-language queries
commands: fabio data-agent update-config --workspace <WS> --id <DA> --instructions "Support group by in GQL"
fabio data-agent query --workspace <WS> --id <DA> --prompt "What is the top product by revenue across all stores?"
steps.notes: The 'Support group by in GQL' instruction improves aggregation. Alternatively, query the ontology directly (its MCP search_ontology tool) with: fabio ontology search --workspace <WS> --id <ONT> --prompt "...".
